question:
Which of the given statements about Vitamin A are correct?

**Statement A :** Beta - carotene is a precursor to Vitamin A.

**Statement B : **Leafy green vegetables and yellow fruits are good sources of Vitamin A.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Statements A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Beta-carotene** is indeed a precursor to Vitamin A. It is a type of carotenoid that the body can convert into Vitamin A as needed.

• **Leafy green vegetables and yellow fruits** are excellent sources of Vitamin A. Foods such as spinach, kale, and carrots are rich in beta-carotene.

• Vitamin A plays a crucial role in maintaining healthy vision, immune function, and skin health.

• Deficiency of Vitamin A can lead to severe health issues, including night blindness and an increased risk of infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Vitamin A**

• It is a fat-soluble vitamin that is crucial for maintaining vision, promoting growth and development, and protecting epithelium and mucous integrity in the body.

• There are two types of Vitamin A found in nature: preformed Vitamin A (retinol and retinyl ester) and provitamin A carotenoids (beta-carotene, alpha-carotene).

• Preformed Vitamin A is found in foods from animal sources, including dairy products, fish, and meat (especially liver).

• Provitamin A carotenoids are abundant in plant-based foods such as fruits and vegetables, with beta-carotene being the most significant.

• **Beta-carotene**

• It is an antioxidant that gives yellow and orange fruits and vegetables their color.

• In the body, beta-carotene is converted into retinol (Vitamin A), which is necessary for healthy skin, mucous membranes, the immune system, and good eye health and vision.

• Beta-carotene is also known for its role in reducing the risk of chronic diseases by neutralizing free radicals.

• **Sources of Vitamin A**

• Animal sources: Liver, fish oils, milk, eggs.

• Plant sources: Leafy green vegetables (spinach, kale), yellow/orange vegetables (carrots, sweet potatoes), yellow fruits (mangoes, apricots).

• Fortified foods: Some cereals and dairy products are fortified with Vitamin A.

• **Health benefits of Vitamin A**

• Maintains healthy vision and prevents night blindness.

• Supports the immune system by maintaining the integrity and function of skin and mucosal cells.

• Promotes growth and development, especially in children.

• Has antioxidant properties that help in reducing the risk of chronic diseases.
